questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chenab Rail Bridge is the world’s highest railway arch bridge.
2. The Anji Bridge, located in Arunachal Pradesh, is India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(a)
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently inaugurated the Chenab and Anji rail bridges in the UT of Jammu and Kashmir.
• The Chenab Rail Bridge is the world’s highest railway arch bridge, located in Jammu & Kashmir, standing 359 meters above the Chenab River.
• Anji Bridge, India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge, is located in the Reasi district of Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.qtext:
Which of the following is/are members of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)?
1. Governor of Reserve Bank of India
2. Chief Economic Adviser
3. Chairman of Securities and Exchange Board of India
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.solution:
(d)
• Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) was established in December 2010 and is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes top financial officials such as the RBI Governor, Finance Secretary, Chief Economic Adviser, and heads of Securities and Exchange
Board of India (SEBI), Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI) and Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).
• It addresses issues related to financial stability, sector development, inter-regulatory
coordination, financial literacy, inclusion, and supervision of large financial entities.

questions.qtext: What does the Gini Index primarily measure?

options.text: Economic growth rate of a country

questions.solution:
(c)
• The Gini index is a measure of the distribution of income across a population.
• A higher Gini index indicates greater inequality, with high-income individuals receiving much
larger percentages of the population’s total income.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements best describes the Trade Deficit?

options.text: It arises when a country purchases more goods from other countries than it exports to them.
It occurs when the government’s revenue expenditure exceeds its revenue receipts.
It is a decrease in the value of an asset over time due to wear and tear.
It is the gap between the fiscal deficit and the interest paid on borrowed funds.

questions.solution:
(a)
• A trade deficit occurs when a country’s imports exceed its exports, resulting in a negative trade balance.
• It includes both goods and services and serves as a key macroeconomic indicator.
• Persistent trade deficits can lead to currency depreciation, job losses, and increased foreign borrowing.

questions.qtext:
Which among the following are the components of the Current Account Balance of a country?
1. Export and import of goods
2. Net income from interest and dividends
3. Net transfers like remittances and foreign aid
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.solution:
(d)
• The Current Account Balance is a key component of a country’s Balance of Payments (BoP) and reflects its transactions with the rest of the world in goods, services, income, and transfers.
• The Current Account comprises trade in goods, trade in services, primary income (investment income), and secondary income (transfers and remittances).
• A surplus in the current account occurs when inflows exceed outflows.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements regarding the Census in India:
1. The first synchronous decennial census in India was conducted in 1881 under the supervision of W.C. Plowden.
2. Independent India’s first census took place in 1951, and since then, it has been conducted in the first year of every decade.
3. The Census of India Act of 1948 specifies exact timing and periodicity of Census.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
(a)
• The first synchronous (simultaneous across regions) decennial census in India was indeed conducted in 1881.
• It was carried out under the supervision of W.C. Plowden, who was then the Census Commissioner of India.
• The first census after independence was held in 1951.
• Since then, India has conducted a decennial census in every first year of the decade.
• The 2021 census was delayed due to COVID-19 but this does not make the statement incorrect.
• The Census Act of 1948 does not mandate any fixed timing or periodicity. It empowers the government to decide when to conduct a census, but does not require it to be every 10 years.

questions.qtext: Which state became the first in India to introduce mobile app-based e-Voting in municipal and byelections?
questions.solution:

With reference to DHRUVA Initiative, consider the following statements:
1. It is being developed by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
2. Its primary goal is to provide a unique digital address for every home in India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(b)
• DHRUVA (Digital Hub for Reference and Unique Virtual Address) is a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) project being developed by the Department of Posts (DoP) in India. Its primary goal is to provide a unique digital address for every home in India.
• Objectives:
– To establish address information management as a foundational public infrastructure.
– To enable effective governance, inclusive service delivery, and enhanced user experience through accurate address sharing.

questions.qtext:
With reference to North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), consider the following statements:
1. The principal decision-making body of NATO is the North Atlantic Council.
2. NATO decisions are made by majority vote among member countries.
3. Finland was the 31st country to join NATO.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• NATO, or the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, is a military alliance of countries.
• The North Atlantic Council, which includes the ambassadors of all member countries, is the principal political decision-making body.
• Decisions within NATO are made on the basis of consensus among member countries. It has 32 member countries, Finland and Sweden became the 31st and 32nd members respectively.
• On signing the Treaty, countries voluntarily commit themselves to participating in the political consultations and military activities of the Organization.

questions.qtext: Recently, which one of the following countries has agreed for the ‘Double Contribution Convention’ with India?
questions.solution:
(a)
• The Double Contribution Convention is a bilateral agreement that prevents Indian workers, temporarily posted to the UK for up to three years, from having to pay social security contributions in both countries simultaneously.
• It applies to both the worker and their employer. It is a broader agreement that includes an
FTA with the UK, recently concluded FTA, benefiting 99% of Indian exports from tariff reductions.
• India’s exports to the U.K. reached $12 billion in FY2024.
• It aims to make it easier for British firms to export whisky, cars, and other products to India, boosting overall trade.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements regarding Financial Action Task Force (FATF):
1. Financial Action Task Force is a treaty-based organization with enforcement powers like the International Criminal Court (ICC).
2. Its recommendations are legally binding on all members.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(d)
• Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is an intergovernmental organization which leads global action to tackle money laundering, terrorist and proliferation financing.
• FATF was established in 1989 by the G7 to examine and develop measures to combat money laundering.
• FATF currently has 39 members, including two regional organizations (European Commission and Gulf Cooperation Council).
• India became a member in 2010.
• It is located at the OECD Headquarters in Paris.

Statement (I): Statement (I): Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) is a monetary policy instrument employed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to maintain short-term interest rate stability.
Statement (II): It is primarily used to absorb surplus liquidity from the banking system.
questions.solution:
(b)
• The Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) is a monetary policy tool. By conducting VRRR auctions, the RBI influences short-term interest rates and ensures they remain close to the policy rate, helping maintain rate stability.
• The VRRR is a liquidity absorption tool. When there is excess liquidity in the banking system (e.g., due to large inflows or government spending), the RBI uses the VRRR to drain out this surplus, thereby avoiding inflationary pressures and maintaining monetary stability.
